'''Astrid Lambrecht''' (born 20 January 1967) is a German physicist who is Director at [[Forschungszentrum Jülich]]. She previously worked as the Deputy Director of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] Institute of Physics.

== Early life and education ==
Lambrecht was born in [[Mülheim]]. She completed her undergraduate studies in physics at the [[University of Duisburg-Essen]] and [[Imperial College London]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |date=2020-01-01 |title=Astrid Lambrecht, la curiosité en partage |url=https://www.refletsdelaphysique.fr/articles/refdp/abs/2020/01/refdp202064p40/refdp202064p40.html |journal=Reflets de la Physique |language=fr |issue=64 |pages=40–41 |doi=10.1051/refdp/202064040 |issn=1953-793X|doi-access=free }}</ref> At Imperial College, she worked alongside [[Peter Knight (physicist)|Peter Knight]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=CV HAL |url=https://cv.archives-ouvertes.fr/astrid-lambrecht |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=cv.archives-ouvertes.fr}}</ref> She moved to [[Paris]] for her doctoral research, studying quantum fluctuations of cold atoms at the [[Kastler–Brossel Laboratory]].<ref name=":1" /> Based in the laboratory of [[Elisabeth Giacobino]], she used an optical cavity and magneto-optic trap to study quantum noise.<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=ATOMES FROIDS ET FLUCTUATIONS QUANTIQUES |publisher=[Editeur inconnu] |date=1995 |place=Lieu de publication inconnu |language=French |first=Astrid |last=Lambrecht|oclc=490256830 }}</ref> She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]]. Lambrecht completed her [[habilitation]] at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]].<ref name=":1" />

== Research and career ==
Lambrecht was appointed to the Institute of Physics at  research leader at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]],{{when|date=November 2022}}<ref name=":1" /> where she studied quantum fluctuations in cold matter.<ref name=":0" /> In particular, she worked on the [[Casimir effect]]. The Casimir effect is exploited in [[microelectromechanical systems]]. At the same time, Lambrecht demonstrated that the Casimir effect has fundamental impacts in biology and chemistry.{{citation needed|date=March 2022}} In 2014, she was made deputy director of the Kastler–Brossel Laboratory, and in 2016, Deputy Scientific Director at the CNRS headquarters.<ref name=":0" /> She was nominated Director of the Institute of Physics in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Communication INP |title=Astrid Lambrecht prend la direction de l'INP {{!}} INP |url=https://www.inp.cnrs.fr/fr/cnrsinfo/astrid-lambrecht-prend-la-direction-de-linp |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=www.inp.cnrs.fr |date=18 July 2018 |language=fr}}</ref> In 2021, Lambrecht joined the Board of Directors at the [[Forschungszentrum Jülich]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Forschungszentrum Jülich – Dr. Astrid Lambrecht |url=https://www.fz-juelich.de/portal/EN/AboutUs/organizational_structure/CompanyBodies/BoardOfDirectors/AstridLambrecht/_node.html |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=www.fz-juelich.de}}</ref>

* 2016 Gentner-Kastler-Prize<ref>{{Cite web |title=Preisträgerinnen und Preisträger |url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise-mit-anderen-organisationen/gentner-kastler-preis-und-medaille/preistraeger |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=DPG |language=en}}</ref>
